options.name: audit
options.setting-help: the SCR audit trail: the sink, the forwarding, the rotation, the kill switch

options.name: audit-log
options.setting-help: SCR audit trail: a file path or - for stdout (the docker/journald way); `none` = no local file (the forward carries the trail); default: the XDG state home (~/.local/state/modbus-scraper/audit.log)
options.help: SCR audit trail: a file path or - for stdout (the docker/journald way); `none` turns the local file off (with a forward spelled that is the remote-only mode); the XDG state home (~/.local/state/modbus-scraper/audit.log) when unset

options.name: audit-forward
options.setting-help: also forward every audit line: the local syslog mirror or a remote collector (the off-box copy)
options.help: also forward the SCR audit trail: syslog (the local socket auto-scan), syslog:/path (an explicit socket), udp://host[:514] (RFC5426, best-effort) or tcp://host[:514] (RFC6587 framing) — the off-box copy carries the per-writer hash chain, so a scheduled search at the collector can alert on a chain break; docs/AUDIT.md

options.name: audit-forward-format

value-help.rfc5424: the syslog envelope, the native line verbatim in the MSG
value-help.cef: the CEF additive wrapping, msg= carries the native line

options.help: the remote forward's envelope: RFC5424 (the default) or CEF — the local syslog forms keep the verbatim send (remote targets only)

options.setting-help: the state dump: the live overrides' file, the restore-on-start

options.name: dump-path
options.setting-help: the state dump file: the live overrides, written on request dump, the graceful shutdown and every dump-interval
options.help: the state dump: the live setting overrides (the poll plan, the caps, the log surface — the tokens apart) as one JSON, written 0600 with an integrity hash (a restore refuses a tampered, unsigned or group-writable dump); dumped on the request dump command, the graceful shutdown and every --dump-interval seconds; loaded on start only with --restore-on-start, on demand with the request restore command

options.name: dump-key
options.setting-help: the key that seals the state dumps (the reload's state file too) (`file:<path>` reads an owner-only file)
options.help: the key that seals the state dumps and the reload's state file: the state rides encrypted (an HMAC-SHA256 counter-mode keystream, authenticated — a restore refuses a wrong or missing key, and a configured key refuses an unsealed dump); the reload re-exec re-resolves the same key, so the state file reads on the other side; no key = the dumps stay 0600 plaintext with the integrity hash a dump path without a key warns at start and on set; the value may be `file:<path>` — the first line of an owner-only 0600 file (a systemd LoadCredential rides as file:/run/credentials/...)

options.name: dump-interval
options.setting-help: seconds between the automatic state dumps (the live setting overrides)

value-help.off: only request dump and the shutdown dump

options.help: seconds between the automatic state dumps, 0 = on request (the request dump command and the shutdown)

options.name: restore-on-start
options.setting-help: the dump loads on start (off: on demand with request restore)
options.help: load the state dump when the daemon starts (needs --dump-path) — the live overrides ride again instead of a cold start; without it the dump loads on demand
